Dolphins 6, Nembe City 0 (22 Oct.) | biggest away win = Nembe City 0, Giwa 4 (16 Nov.) | highest scoring = Warri Wolves 7, Crown 1 (22 Oct.) | longest wins = | longest unbeaten = Sharks F.C. – 10 games (19 April to 1 June) | longest winless = | longest losses = | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | average attendance = | prevseason = [[2013 Nigeria Premier League|2013]] | nextseason = [[2015 Nigeria Professional Football League|2015]] }} The '''2014 Nigeria Professional Football League''' was the 43rd season of the competition since its inception, and the 24th since the rebranding of the league as the "Professional League". The season was scheduled to kick off on November 22, about one month after the conclusion of the 2013 season.{{Cite web |url=http://www.mtnfootball.com/africa/nigeria/premier-league/news/2013/oct/09-new-nigeria-league-season-kicks-off-nov-22.html |title=New Nigeria league season kicks off Nov 22 |access-date=2013-10-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131009175503/http://www.mtnfootball.com/africa/nigeria/premier-league/news/2013/oct/09-new-nigeria-league-season-kicks-off-nov-22.html |archive-date=2013-10-09 |url-status=dead }} However, on that date the league's start was postponed to mid-February until after the [[2014 African Nations Championship]] and to allow the teams to complete all their FIFA licensing.{{Cite web|url=http://www.9jafootball.com/newspage.php?newssplash=Nigeria+football+league+p|title=9jafootball.com|website=www.9jafootball.com|accessdate=6 August 2023}} It was delayed again until March. ==Clubs== Sixteen teams from the [[2013 Nigeria Premier League|previous season]] and four teams promoted from the [[Nigeria National League]] ([[Crown F.C.]], [[Giwa FC]], [[Taraba F.C.]] and [[Abia Warriors F.C.]]) are participating in this season. Stars F.C.]] was involved in an accident on the road between Ijebu-Ode and Akure. Five players and the team masseur went to the hospital with serious injuries. However, nobody was killed.{{Cite web |url=http://www.mtnfootball.com/africa/nigeria/premier-league/news/2013/dec/were-lucky-to-be-alive-sunshine-player.html |title=We're lucky to be alive - Sunshine player |access-date=2014-02-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302041413/http://www.mtnfootball.com/africa/nigeria/premier-league/news/2013/dec/were-lucky-to-be-alive-sunshine-player.html |archive-date=2014-03-02 |url-status=dead }} *- On the eve of the league start, Giwa F.C. and Nembe City (the last two [[Nigeria National League]] champions and the league's only two privately funded clubs) were withdrawn from league fixtures by the LMC for failing to provide guarantees of the minimum salary for players, leaving the league at 18 teams.{{Cite web|url=http://www.supersport.com/football/nigeria/news/140307/Giwa_FC_Nembe_City_thrown_out_of_NPFL|title=Giwa, Nembe City thrown out of NPFL (supersport.com)|accessdate=6 August 2023}} Both teams appealed to be reinstated on March 20. Giwa was admitted back on the 2nd of April and Nembe City was readmitted the next day.{{Cite web|url=http://www.supersport.com/football/nigeria/news/140402/Giwa_FC_readmitted_into_NPFL|title = Giwa FC re-admitted into NPFL}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.supersport.com/football/nigeria/news/140403/Nembe_City_return_to_NPFL|title = Nembe City return to NPFL}} *- After the Week 1 games, Abia Warriors refused to travel to Maiduguri to play El-Kanemi Warriors, citing fears for safety after recent Boko Haram attacks. The league then refused to sanction games there, and El Kanemi nominally agreed to move games this season to Kano.{{Cite web |url=http://www.mtnfootball.com/africa/nigeria/premier-league/news/2014/mar/14-el-kanemi-opt-for-kano.html |title = El Kanemi opt for Kano - MTNFootball |access-date=2014-03-15
